newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKMA pumps HK$1.4 bln more into interbank market.
newsitem.headline: HKMA pumps HK$1.4 bln more into interbank market.

text.p: Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the territory's defacto central bank, said it pumped another HK$1.4 billion into the interbank market, bringing the total money injection on Friday to HK$2.4 billion.
The authority added HK$1.0 billion into the market earlier to soothe the tightness in the market.
"The move is in response to the strong demand sparked by a stock run and the month-end effect," a HKMA spokesman.
He said HKMA made the first injection at 11:00 am (0300 gmt) when overnight rate was at 6.375 percent and a second move around midday as overnights still stayed above six percent.
"The overight rate has now moved lower to 5-13/16 percent," the spokesman said.
Dealers said short-term money rates should ease further later in the day due to the hefty money injections.
Much of the demand was from the public offer of 68 million shares in Nam Fong International Holdings Ltd, which closed at noon on Friday and was expected to be heavily oversubscribed.
The stock money receiving bank failed to turn the money back to the market swiftly also escalated the problem, one dealer said. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6369
